![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/25d4f77a3f596202229581e06d88a9e3bdd84dc6b8b7e14b6f46b3b3d2f125d2.png)

Consider the phase portrait for a decoupled system above.
Which of the following systems could correspond to the given portrait?

I. $\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-5x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=6y(t)\end{aligned}$

II. $\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=5x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=6y(t)\end{aligned}$

III. $\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=5x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-6y(t)\end{aligned}$

IV. $\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-5x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-6y(t)\end{aligned}$
question.worked_solution:
Writing a decoupled system in matrix form, we have
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/50b547a3223fe85dde50b06d78ee35bfff49d95c43a4ebadcc2d1007ac041eb1.svg)
where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/ee1bb1b6a9869493ae3bcfaa42d63d07b6054aaa19f25c9fa8a2665e9642e0be.svg)

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are parallel to the axes. These correspond to so-called straight-line solutions of the form
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/853be349a48d204b073b1ad3aaa709df082bd7fa5163aec09d5364836918a9e6.svg)

Now, notice that:

- The tangents along the $x$-axis are pointing toward the origin, meaning that the solutions of the form 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/5903874b33d77f242d725ad16fffef59ee24e1bde4210128ed590031ddc43e99.svg)
must approach the origin as $t \to \infty.$ So, we must have $\lambda_1 < 0.$

- The tangents along the $y$-axis are also pointing toward the origin, meaning that the solutions of the form 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/856d5a86b76c30e0601803216465f29a1e3bd7fb993a58ee6ba85ba7c0627fd9.svg)
must also approach the origin as $t \to \infty.$ So, we must have $\lambda_2 < 0.$

Among the options, the only system that satisfies $\lambda_1 < 0$ and $\lambda_2 < 0$ is the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-5x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-6y(t)\end{aligned}
$$
